section_path_text: Ship Prices Rise: Will Rates Make up the Difference?
summary: Ship Prices Rise: Will Rates Make up the Difference? What every ship owner knows post the 1973 Middle East oil crisis is that he really never knows. And with VLCC newbuilding prices the highest they've been in nearly 10 years, wild cards such as an oil crisis are decidedly less palatable to the taste.

children.summary: This market is seeing second hand modern double-hull ship prices on par with newbuilding prices, as in the graph on the next page. This is associated with owners wanting to buy an existing ship to take advantage of current high rates rather than wait for one to be built.

children.title: Second Hand Prices
children.summary: China May as Well Build Ships, They're Taking all the Steel Steel prices have increased by $140 during the past two years as shown below. China's need for steel is blamed - or alternatively credited - for the increase.

children.title: US$/ton
children.summary: Suezmaxes, Aframaxes and Panamaxes are seeing the same type of price increases. A Suezmax newbuilding is quoted at just over $57 million this month, the highest quote in the past decade.

children.summary: Naturally owners want to make sure their investment in a newbuilding is profitable and hope that rates will be high. Shipbuilding prices may decline with more competition from Chinese shipyards, as was seen in the early 1990s when Korean shipyards moved into the picture.
